newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile posts $499 mln January-May trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: Chile posts $499 mln January-May trade surplus.

text.p: Chile reported a $499 million trade surplus in the first six months of the year, down from $605 million in the same period last year, said the Central Bank in its monthly report.
Bank figures showed a $56 million trade deficit last month as the result of imports of $1.37 billion and exports of $1.32 billion.
"This result is explained in large measure by the fall in the value of exports compared with the same month 1996, even though imports also dropped," said the report.
In May last year, Chile reported imports of $1.39 billion and exports of $1.49 billion.
The fall in exports in May was mainly the result of a 44 percent drop in the foreign sales of fresh fruit, said the report.
But the figure for fresh fruit exports was preliminary and could be revised when the bank has more details of the prices Chilean fruit fetched abroad, it said.
Raw and bleached wood pulp exports fell 41 percent and 37 percent respectively last month despite an increase in cellulose prices.

"These figures contrast sharply with the dynamism wood pulp shipments have shown so far this year," said the report, adding cumulative raw pulp exports were 20 percent higher than in 1996 and bleached pulp shipments were up 10 percent.
The main reason for the fall last month was the high base of comparison as wood pulp exports in May last year were exceptionally high, it said.
Copper exports fell three percent last month with a rise in export volumes unable to counteract a five percent fall in world prices over the year.
Imports fell one percent over the last year as the result of a drop in imports of capital and intermediate goods. Consumer goods imports grew 1.5 percent in May.
The following are details of Chile's main exports and imports in May.
